The MGO tank sits outside Max_ROB_MT and is taken as 0.40 x Max_ROB_MT by scripts/gen-vessel-movement.mjs, raised from 0.20 when ECA coverage extended to the North Sea/Channel and Mediterranean SOx zones (their merged windows exceeded the original ~4.4-day autonomy; checkInvariants found the tightest case on MEDI's KOTA PUSAKA at Valencia). Applies to the vessels in METHANOL_VESSELS (scripts/gen-vessel-movement.mjs, 3 vessels: KOTA SEGAR, KOTA SEJARAH, ASTERIOS) only; their ECA-compliance tank is methanol instead of MGO, so MGO_Max_ROB_MT above does not apply to them and this row does not apply to anyone else. MEOH_MAX_RATIO = MGO_MAX_RATIO x (42.7 / 19.9) x 2.3: methanol carries under half MGO's energy per tonne (data/emissions/energy_per_mt.csv), so the base tank needs proportionally more mass for the same days of ECA-window autonomy; the x2.3 buffer was tried for an Asia-Europe methanol candidate (KOTA LEKAS/EUROMED) and still wasn't enough (Ningbo is MEOH's only supply port, so a Europe-crossing vessel gets one fill per loop to cover the whole round trip) — MEOH stayed intra-Asia-only despite the raised ratio. See data/README.md, 'A second ECA-compliance grade' and 'Widening compliance-fuel coverage'.

Applies to the vessels in LNG_VESSELS (scripts/gen-vessel-movement.mjs, 23 vessels — 16 intra-Asia across CVI/KCS/KCI/NCI/VCS/CCS, plus 7 Asia-Europe: KOTA EBONY/AE1, KOTA ELAN/AE2, KOTA PLUMBAGO/AE3, KOTA PELANGI+KOTA PURI/AE5, KOTA LEMBAH+KOTA LAMBAI/EUROMED) only; their ECA-compliance tank is LNG instead of MGO, so MGO_Max_ROB_MT above does not apply to them and this row does not apply to anyone else. LNG_MAX_RATIO = MGO_MAX_RATIO x (42.7 / 48.0) x 2.3: LNG carries more energy per tonne than MGO (data/emissions/energy_per_mt.csv), so the base ratio needs less mass than MGO's — the opposite direction from MEOH; the x2.3 buffer on top was needed once LNG_VESSELS extended onto Asia-Europe services, whose only LNG supply calls are in Asia, so the tank must survive the whole Europe-side ECA exposure on one fill. Tuned empirically in steps (2x, 2.1x, 2.3x) against checkInvariants — the failure margin did not shrink monotonically with the ratio, so this figure is not provably minimal, just the smallest tried that cleared every kept candidate. Real cryogenic LNG tanks are bulkier per unit energy than this mass ratio implies (Type-C tank insulation and pressure-vessel overhead); this model tracks autonomy-days, not volume. See data/README.md, 'A second ECA-compliance grade' and 'Widening compliance-fuel coverage'.
Derived: LNG_Max_ROB_MT / 3, mirroring MGO_Min_ROB_MT / MGO_Max_ROB_MT. Applies only to the vessels in LNG_VESSELS.
Derived: LNG_Max_ROB_MT / 2, mirroring MGO_Bunkering_Trigger_MT / MGO_Max_ROB_MT. Applies only to the vessels in LNG_VESSELS.

Applies to the vessels in B40_VESSELS (scripts/gen-vessel-movement.mjs) — KOTA SAHABAT, KOTA SALAM, KOTA SEMPENA, KOTA SINGA — only; their ECA-compliance tank is the Pertamina B40 biofuel blend (60% MGO / 40% FAME) instead of plain MGO, so MGO_Max_ROB_MT above does not apply to them and this row does not apply to anyone else. B40_MAX_RATIO = MGO_MAX_RATIO x (42.7 / 40.6): B40 carries marginally less energy per tonne than pure MGO (data/emissions/energy_per_mt.csv), so the tank is marginally larger for equal autonomy. See data/README.md, 'A second ECA-compliance grade' and 'Widening compliance-fuel coverage'.
